::: {.eyebrow}
Curiosity · INEGI, Encuesta Intercensal 2025 · Public microdata
:::

A national average weights every person equally. That is what makes it the right
number for a question about people, and the wrong one for a question about
places. If half a country's population lives in a handful of large cities, the
national average resembles those cities. It does not resemble the typical town.

The two are different quantities. **A population-weighted average answers "what
happens to the average person"; an average across places answers "what happens in
the average place."** Almost always the first gets computed and the second gets
reported. They can sit thirty points apart.

Mexico's 2025 intercensal survey, published in September 2026, makes the gap easy
to see. It interviewed about seven million dwellings, which is enough to estimate
each of the country's 2,478 municipalities separately.

## Before the map: the whole country

The survey asks about seven employment benefits, and it asks only of people who
work for an employer (not the self-employed, who were never posed the question).
Among those 40.9 million people, this is the country:

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
nacional = FileAttachment("../../data/prestaciones-nacional.csv").csv({ typed: true })
municipios = FileAttachment("../../data/prestaciones-municipios.csv").csv({ typed: true })
reparto = FileAttachment("../../data/prestaciones-reparto.csv").csv({ typed: true })
mx = FileAttachment("../../data/mx-municipios-2025.json").json()

// Una rampa secuencial por prestación, de un solo tono, como en la curiosidad de
// mascotas: con una rampa compartida, cambiar de prestación solo cambiaba el
// sombreado y el cambio se perdía. El dominio sí es fijo (0-90%) para que las
// siete se puedan comparar entre ellas.
medidas = ({
  aguinaldo:        { nombre: "Year-end bonus", etiqueta: "Receives a year-end bonus (%)", esquema: "YlGnBu" },
  vacaciones:       { nombre: "Paid holiday", etiqueta: "Receives paid holiday (%)", esquema: "BuPu" },
  servicio_medico:  { nombre: "Health coverage", etiqueta: "Has health coverage through the job (%)", esquema: "YlOrBr" },
  incap_sueldo:     { nombre: "Paid sick leave", etiqueta: "Receives paid sick leave (%)", esquema: "PuBuGn" },
  sar_afore:        { nombre: "Retirement saving", etiqueta: "Has retirement saving (%)", esquema: "Purples" },
  credito_vivienda: { nombre: "Housing credit", etiqueta: "Has housing credit (%)", esquema: "Greens" },
  utilidades:       { nombre: "Profit sharing", etiqueta: "Receives profit sharing (%)", esquema: "OrRd" }
})

munFeatures = topojson.feature(mx, mx.objects.municipalities).features
// Las fronteras estatales salen de los MISMOS arcos municipales, así que no
// pueden quedar desalineadas y no cuestan bytes adicionales.
fronterasEstatales = topojson.mesh(mx, mx.objects.municipalities,
  (a, b) => a.properties.state_code !== b.properties.state_code)
contornoPais = topojson.mesh(mx, mx.objects.municipalities, (a, b) => a === b)

// `typed: true` convierte "01001" en el número 1001 y el join falla en
// silencio (§13, bug 3). La llave se normaliza a texto de 5 dígitos.
porCvegeo = new Map(municipios.map(d => [String(d.cvegeo).padStart(5, "0"), d]))
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
tablaNacional = Inputs.table(nacional, {
  columns: ["prestacion", "nacional", "mediana_municipal", "pct_debajo"],
  header: {
    prestacion: "Benefit",
    nacional: "National (%)",
    mediana_municipal: "Median municipality (%)",
    pct_debajo: "Municipalities below the national figure (%)"
  },
  format: { prestacion: d => medidas[d].nombre },
  rows: 7,
  layout: "auto"
})
```

Two things stand out before any geography. Profit sharing is last at 42.7% and
the year-end bonus is first at 64.2%, and **both are legal obligations, not
employer favours**. Twenty-two points separate two entitlements that the law
treats identically, which says less about what the law requires than about what
gets complied with and what workers know they are owed.

And the distribution is not a gradient. It is two blocks:

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  width: 640, height: 260, marginLeft: 46, marginBottom: 42,
  style: { background: "transparent", fontFamily: "IBM Plex Sans, sans-serif", fontSize: "12px", color: "var(--ink)" },
  x: { label: "Number of the seven benefits →", tickFormat: d => d, domain: [-0.5, 7.5] },
  y: { label: "% of employees", grid: true },
  marks: [
    Plot.rectY(reparto, { x: "k", y: "share", interval: 1, fill: "var(--ink)", fillOpacity: 0.78 }),
    Plot.ruleY([0], { stroke: "var(--ink)", strokeOpacity: 0.4 })
  ]
})
```

**36.4% have all seven and 33.0% have none.** Only 2.9% sit at the exact middle
of the scale. One in three employees in Mexico (13.5 million people) works for
an employer with no year-end bonus, no paid holiday, no health coverage and no
retirement saving. The mean, 3.77 of seven, describes almost nobody.

## Now the map

Everything above is an average of people. The map changes the unit: each polygon
is one municipality, and they all weigh the same whether two thousand people live
there or two million.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof medida_sel = Inputs.radio(Object.keys(medidas), {
  value: "aguinaldo",
  label: "Benefit",
  format: d => medidas[d].nombre
})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
etiquetaMapa = medidas[medida_sel].etiqueta
esquemaMapa = medidas[medida_sel].esquema
nacionalMapa = nacional.find(d => d.prestacion === medida_sel)

// La función de la gráfica NO lee el selector: recibe filas, etiqueta y esquema.
// Es la forma que ya usan data-informality.qmd y la curiosidad de mascotas.
graficaMapa = (clave, etiqueta, esquema, { width = 700 } = {}) => {
  const valor = f => {
    const d = porCvegeo.get(f.properties.CVEGEO);
    return d ? d[clave] : undefined;
  };
  const impreciso = f => {
    const d = porCvegeo.get(f.properties.CVEGEO);
    return d ? d["p_" + clave] === 0 : false;
  };
  const figura = Plot.plot({
    width, height: Math.round(width * 0.62),
    projection: { type: "mercator", domain: { type: "FeatureCollection", features: munFeatures } },
    style: { background: "transparent", fontFamily: "IBM Plex Sans, sans-serif", fontSize: "12px", color: "var(--ink)" },
    color: {
      type: "quantize", n: 7, scheme: esquema, domain: [0, 0.9],
      label: etiqueta, legend: true, tickFormat: d => (100 * d).toFixed(0) + "%",
      unknown: "transparent"
    },
    marks: [
      Plot.geo(munFeatures, {
        fill: valor, stroke: "var(--rule)", strokeWidth: 0.12, tip: true,
        title: f => {
          const d = porCvegeo.get(f.properties.CVEGEO);
          if (!d) return `${f.properties.NOMGEO}\nsample too small to publish`;
          const v = d[clave];
          return `${d.municipio}, ${d.entidad}\n${etiqueta}: ${(100 * v).toFixed(1)}%` +
                 (d["p_" + clave] === 1 ? "" : "  (imprecise)");
        }
      }),
      Plot.geo(munFeatures.filter(impreciso), { fill: "url(#rayas)", stroke: "none" }),
      Plot.geo(fronterasEstatales, { stroke: "var(--ink)", strokeWidth: 0.45, strokeOpacity: 0.4 }),
      Plot.geo(contornoPais, { stroke: "var(--ink)", strokeWidth: 0.7, strokeOpacity: 0.65 })
    ]
  });
  // El rayado va como patrón SVG inyectado después de que Plot arma la figura.
  const svg = figura.tagName === "svg" ? figura : figura.querySelector("svg");
  const defs = d3.select(svg).insert("defs", ":first-child");
  defs.append("pattern")
    .attr("id", "rayas").attr("width", 3.2).attr("height", 3.2)
    .attr("patternUnits", "userSpaceOnUse").attr("patternTransform", "rotate(45)")
    .append("line")
      .attr("x1", 0).attr("y1", 0).attr("x2", 0).attr("y2", 3.2)
      .attr("stroke", "var(--plot-background)").attr("stroke-width", 1.3).attr("stroke-opacity", 0.85);
  return figura;
}
```

::: {.data-panel}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
graficaMapa(medida_sel, etiquetaMapa, esquemaMapa)
```

:::

Hatched municipalities are the ones whose estimate is imprecise. They are shown
anyway, in full colour, for a reason the last section explains.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
graficaDistribucion = (clave, nac, { width = 700 } = {}) => {
  const vals = municipios.map(d => d[clave]).filter(v => v != null);
  const mediana = d3.median(vals);
  return Plot.plot({
    width, height: 170, marginLeft: 20, marginRight: 20, marginTop: 52, marginBottom: 38,
    style: { background: "transparent", fontFamily: "IBM Plex Sans, sans-serif", fontSize: "12px", color: "var(--ink)" },
    x: { domain: [0, 0.9], label: "Coverage in the municipality →", tickFormat: d => (100 * d).toFixed(0) + "%", grid: true },
    y: { axis: null },
    marks: [
      Plot.dot(vals, Plot.dodgeY({ anchor: "bottom", padding: 0.35 },
        { x: d => d, r: 2, fill: "var(--ink)", fillOpacity: 0.22 })),
      Plot.ruleX([mediana], { stroke: "var(--ink)", strokeWidth: 1.5 }),
      Plot.ruleX([nac.nacional / 100], { stroke: "var(--clay)", strokeWidth: 2 }),
      // Dos renglones distintos, o las etiquetas se enciman a ancho de teléfono.
      Plot.text([`median municipality ${(100 * mediana).toFixed(1)}%`], {
        x: mediana, frameAnchor: "top", dy: -34, fontSize: 12, fill: "var(--ink)",
        textAnchor: mediana < 0.45 ? "start" : "end", dx: mediana < 0.45 ? 6 : -6
      }),
      Plot.text([`national figure ${nac.nacional.toFixed(1)}%`], {
        x: nac.nacional / 100, frameAnchor: "top", dy: -16, fontSize: 12, fill: "var(--clay)",
        textAnchor: nac.nacional / 100 < 0.45 ? "start" : "end", dx: nac.nacional / 100 < 0.45 ? 6 : -6
      })
    ]
  });
}
```

::: {.data-panel}

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
graficaDistribucion(medida_sel, nacionalMapa)
```

:::

Each dot is one of the 2,471 municipalities with an estimate. The national figure
sits above ${nacionalMapa.pct_debajo} of every 100 of them. For the year-end
bonus the median municipality is at 33.8% against a national 64.2%: thirty points
of distance, and not a calculation error. The national figure weights people; the
map weights places.

## Why some municipalities are hatched

A survey estimate carries sampling error, and the usual way to summarise it is
the coefficient of variation: the standard error divided by the estimate itself.
INEGI publishes a municipal figure when that ratio stays under 15% and withholds
it when it does not. It is a sensible rule and here it is a trap.

The coefficient of variation carries the estimate in its denominator, so it grows
whenever coverage is low, even if the error does not change. In these data the
correlation between coverage and the coefficient of variation is **−0.61**.
Sorting municipalities into five groups by precision, the median coverage of the
year-end bonus falls from 65% in the most precise group to 12% in the least, and
only 13% of that last group clears the 15% bar.

So hiding the imprecise estimates does not remove noise scattered at random. It
removes, almost exactly, the municipalities where the benefit is rarest. The map
would look cleaner and say something false. Hiding them would raise the median
municipality by between 5.3 and 8.9 points depending on the benefit; for profit
sharing the median would go from 10.8% to 19.7%, nearly double, without a single
number being miscalculated.

That is why this map draws them. The hatching does not mean "we don't know". It
means "we know it is very little, and we know it loosely." A reader who treats
hatching as missing data would invert the conclusion of the page.

<details class="abstract">
<summary>How this is built</summary>

**Source:** INEGI, Encuesta Intercensal 2025; microdata published
22 September 2026. Universe: people aged 15 and over, employed and working for an
employer. The survey asks these seven questions only of that group, so **this does
not measure informality** and is not comparable to the rate ENOE publishes.
Estimated with the survey's own design (single-stage, stratified, clustered),
using the strata and primary sampling units INEGI publishes. Municipal medians on
this page are computed over all 2,471 municipalities with an estimate, not only
the precise ones, for the reason given above. Geometry: the Marco Geoestadístico
of the Encuesta Intercensal 2025 itself, with the 2,478 municipalities in force at
the time of the survey; seven are left uncoloured because INEGI did not reach
minimum coverage there and publishes only dwellings and population. Descriptive
and exploratory, and unrelated to the author's work at any institution.

The script that turns the validated estimates into the files this page reads is
[`scripts/09-curiosities-prestaciones.R`](https://github.com/alainpin/alainpineda/blob/main/scripts/09-curiosities-prestaciones.R)
in this site's public repository.

</details>
